rules.title: Project policy is valid
rules.description: The project policy conforms to the portable policy contract.

rules.title: Declared and observed architecture agree
rules.description: Declared modules, hosts, projects, and project names match repository observation.

rules.title: Modules have semantic contracts
rules.description: Every observed module has a schema-valid semantic contract and local AGENTS.md router.

rules.title: Module identity matches its root
rules.description: A module contract id is the normalized name of its module root.

rules.title: Modules represent functional capabilities
rules.description: Technical categories are not represented as product modules.

rules.title: Application behavior has a cohesive feature owner
rules.description: Observed feature roots match policy; semantic cohesion is surfaced for review.

rules.title: Hosts contain only adapters and composition
rules.description: Host source is confined to explicitly declared adapter and composition paths.

rules.title: Modules do not depend on hosts
rules.description: No module-owned project has a direct or transitive dependency on a host-owned project.

rules.title: Cross-module access uses public contracts
rules.description: A cross-module project dependency targets a declared contract boundary.

rules.title: Project dependencies are authorized
rules.description: Every observed project dependency is explicitly allowed by project policy.

rules.title: Authoritative data has one owner
rules.description: Declared ownership is unique and observed writes are reviewed when an analyzer is unavailable.

rules.title: Speculative structure is prohibited
rules.description: Catch-all directories and generated structural fields in semantic contracts are prohibited; boundary necessity remains reviewable.

rules.title: Architectural references resolve
rules.description: Invariant and ADR references from module contracts resolve to existing documents and headings.

rules.title: Waivers are explicit and valid
rules.description: Waivers reference known rules, existing authorities, valid scopes, and unexpired decisions.
